_doc: A GT2 (2MGT) timing belt, 6 mm wide, from Gates's figures for its PowerGrip GT3 2MGT belt, which runs in GT2 sprockets. Unbranded hobby GT2 belt, which is what is usually bought, shares the pitch and profile but its cord is unknown, so its stiffness is community until measured: the only published test found (Wang et al., Robotics 2018, doi 10.3390/robotics7040075) could not be read here. Stiffness is the tension for a strain, the Gates figure: use it as stretch = tension * length / stiffness.
name: gt2-belt-6

pitch.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

width.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

pitch_line_offset.rule: From the pitch diameter to the outside of the teeth, each side: half of Gates's pitch minus outside diameter on a 20 tooth sprocket, (0.501 - 0.481) / 2 in
pitch_line_offset.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Sprocket Specification Tables, 2mm pitch, 2MR-20S-06

stiffness.rule: Tension per unit strain of the 6 mm belt: Gates gives 3.8 lb for 0.1% elongation (fibreglass cord)
stiffness.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

stiffness_per_width.rule: The same per mm of belt width: Gates gives 2.6 lb at 4 mm, 3.8 lb at 6 mm, 5.7 lb at 9 mm for 0.1% elongation
stiffness_per_width.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

rated_tension.rule: Rated working tension (Ta), 39 lb on 14 to 45 grooves, 38 lb on 12
rated_tension.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

breaking_strength.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table 6, long-length belting, LL2MGT06

min_static_tension.rule: Minimum static tension per span, 2.1 lb
min_static_tension.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, engineering section, Tst table

min_inside_idler_grooves.rule: Smallest toothed idler running inside the belt
min_inside_idler_grooves.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table of minimum idlers

min_backside_idler_diameter.rule: Smallest idler on the belt's back, 0.50 in
min_backside_idler_diameter.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table of minimum idlers

min_flat_idler_diameter.rule: Smallest smooth idler inside the belt, on its teeth, 1.00 in. A hobby 18 mm smooth idler is under this if it runs on the teeth, so run it on the back
min_flat_idler_diameter.source: Gates Light Power and Precision Belt Drive Design Manual, copy at https://www.maxiparts.com.au/Documents/Supplier/Gates/light-power-and-precision-manual.pdf, Table of minimum idlers
